**Finding re-submitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

To be straightforward: there was no substantive defect to repair on this pass. Every point in the verifier's feedback affirms the finding — the compliant (not `missing`) classification, the evidence of absence, the reading of p0066, the absence of a redline, and expressly that the two failed deterministic checks are inapplicable. I re-submitted the finding with tightened wording only; the status, cited paragraphs, and quote are unchanged.

The one recurring signal, `general-solicitation carve-out present: failed`, will not clear on any redraft, and it should not. That check looks for carve-out wording inside a non-solicit clause. This Agreement has no non-solicit clause, so there is no text that could ever satisfy it. The only way to make that check pass would be to draft a non-solicitation covenant binding the Associated Press and then equip it with a carve-out — which would create a restriction our client does not currently carry, in direct conflict with the rule's preferred position. I am not making that edit.

Bottom line on the merits: Kubient's paper imposes no hiring or solicitation restriction on the Associated Press, which is the best available outcome under NOSOLICIT. The fallback ceiling is recorded in the finding in case Kubient raises the point in negotiation. I'd treat this rule as closed and recommend the inapplicable-check flag be dispositioned as a scoring artifact rather than routed for further redrafting.
